program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The binding is incomplete (`(...)`) and the node’s question/criteria are not represented in the supplied variable. Repair the typed node so it explicitly evaluates the requested mug’s position against the headphones in the edited image, using the source only to establish whether there was movement. Preserve the distinction between complete (now right of the headphones), partial (moved rightward but not yet right of them), absent (no progress), and unknown (insufficient visual evidence); do not equate any right-of result with full task completion without checking the requested change. The traces all confidently report complete, but the edited image visibly contains multiple mugs: one near the headphones and another to their right, while the source has one mug. This makes object identity/binding and whether the original mug was moved versus duplicated or replaced material ambiguity. Require evidence to identify the source mug across images and assess its displacement, rather than selecting whichever edited mug satisfies the relation. The source-to-edited comparison supports investigating partial progress, but the reference label is aggregate guidance, not atomic ground truth; do not force partial or infer an unshown edit. Repeated identical high-confidence traces are not independent confirmation. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; address the visual identity and progress criterion.
